title: Dry-Room Handoff, Holds and Reconstructable Shift Records

content.overview: A harvest handoff is complete only when the receiving role can reconstruct what arrived, where it came from, what quantity and condition were recorded, what was held or unresolved, and what requires follow-up. This lesson integrates harvest work status, dry-room receiving, environmental and product-condition notes, discrepancy records and shift communication. Learners practice truthful partial-completion records instead of marking the entire harvest complete when a lot, rack, quantity or quality question remains open.

vocabulary.definition: The controlled transfer of material identity, location, quantity, condition, work status and unresolved issues to the receiving role or shift.
A truthful status showing that some assigned work is complete while an identified portion remains held, unresolved or not performed.
A controlled record of a deviation, discrepancy, hold, abnormal condition or incomplete work that requires follow-up.
The ability of another qualified person to determine what occurred, to which material, where and when, what changed and what remains open.

sections.title: Handoff separates completed from unresolved work
sections.body: State which rooms, batches, containers or racks were successfully received and which remain held, mismatched, unavailable or incomplete. A harvest can be partially complete without falsifying the entire work order as finished.

sections.title: Postharvest condition is linked to identity and location
sections.body: Record the dry-room rack or location, supplied environmental information and observed product condition for the correct identified lot. One nonuniform rack or suspect container is documented at its actual scope rather than generalized automatically to the entire room.

sections.title: Uncertainty stays visible
sections.body: If root cause, final disposition, release status or a quantity discrepancy remains unresolved, state that directly. Technician I should not convert an unresolved condition into a guessed explanation or release decision simply to create a clean handoff.

sections.title: Receiving records close the transition
sections.body: The handoff should allow the receiving role to connect source material, harvest output, destination, quantity, hold status, condition note, actions already taken, escalation and next required action. This closes the operational transition without erasing the open issues that still need qualified review.

workedExamples: Three containers are received normally while one is held for suspect contamination. The handoff lists the received locations and quantities separately from the held container and identifies the required review.

A rack’s environmental condition is outside the supplied expectation at shift end. The technician records the identified rack/lot, reading or observation, notification and follow-up requirement without claiming the batch is ruined or independently changing protected control strategy.
commonMistakes: Writing ‘harvest complete’ when a container or discrepancy remains unresolved.
Recording a dry-room condition without linking it to the correct rack or lot.
Replacing an unresolved hold with a guessed release/disposition decision.
Leaving the next shift to reconstruct quantity or location from memory.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a full harvest-to-dry-room packet with normal receiving, one held container, one weight discrepancy, one unavailable destination and one rack requiring environmental follow-up. Produce the harvest record, genealogy map, receiving record, discrepancy/hold record and final handoff.
content.summary: A strong harvest handoff transfers facts, not just material. Technician I preserves identity, quantity, location, condition, work status, holds, discrepancies, escalation and follow-up so the next qualified person can continue the postharvest process without guessing.

blocks.title: Harvest-to-dry-room handoff record
blocks.description: A complete handoff keeps normal receiving, exceptions and unresolved work visible at the same time.

fields.label: Authorization / source identity
fields.value: Harvest work order plus room, plant, batch or lot identity

fields.label: Output identity / destination
fields.value: Harvest container or lot identifier and verified dry-room rack/location

fields.label: Quantity
fields.value: Outgoing and receiving count/weight with units and reconciliation status

fields.label: Condition / environment
fields.value: Required product-condition or dry-room observation tied to the correct lot/location

fields.label: Sanitation / hold status
fields.value: Clean-handling confirmation plus any isolated or held material

fields.label: Deviation / discrepancy
fields.value: Identity, quantity, destination, contamination or equipment issue that remains open

fields.label: Action / escalation
fields.value: Authorized step taken and person/role notified

fields.label: Next action
fields.value: Follow-up required by the receiving shift or qualified reviewer

blocks.title: Source-to-output harvest genealogy
blocks.alt: Source batch linked through a harvest transformation event to multiple identified receiving outputs and destinations, including a held output that remains part of the traceability chain.
blocks.caption: The receiving role should be able to trace every output back to its source transformation, including held material.

blocks.title: Quantity reconciliation and discrepancy control
blocks.alt: Outgoing and receiving quantities remain as separate original records when they differ and are routed into a controlled discrepancy process rather than edited to agree.
blocks.caption: A handoff can remain partially open while a quantity discrepancy is investigated; original evidence stays intact.

blocks.title: Harvest-to-dry-room reconstructable handoff
blocks.alt: Structured dry-room handoff organizing source and output identity, destination, quantity and reconciliation, condition, sanitation or hold state, deviation, escalation and next action.
blocks.caption: A complete handoff makes both completed work and unresolved conditions reconstructable for the receiving shift.

blocks.body: Course 006 supports PRACTICAL-TECH1-F — Harvest-to-Dry-Room Handoff. Passing the written course assessment does not replace the practical demonstration of sanitation, traceability, quantity reconciliation, receiving judgment and handoff performance.

blocks.title: Release authority boundary
blocks.body: Technician I records receiving status, holds, deviations and follow-up. This course does not confer independent product release, disposition or final quality-acceptance authority.
